bib.title: Deep Visual-Semantic Alignments for Generating Image Descriptions

question: How can image-sentence datasets be used as weak labels to align sentence snippets with image regions and then generate descriptions of images and regions?
hypothesis: Treating sentences as weak labels for unknown image locations lets a BRNN-CNN alignment model and a multimodal RNN beat retrieval baselines.
contributions: A deep network that infers latent alignment between sentence segments and image regions via a multimodal embedding and structured objective, surpassing state of the art in image-sentence retrieval
A multimodal RNN that generates image descriptions, outperforming retrieval baselines on full images and on a new region-level annotation dataset

method.summary: Stage 1: RCNN region features (20 per image) and a BRNN over words are embedded in one space and trained with a max-margin ranking loss using score S_kl = sum_t max_i v_i^T s_t; a chain MRF decodes word-to-region alignments. Stage 2: a simple multimodal RNN, conditioned on the image at step 1 only, is trained on full images (VGGNet features) or on inferred region-snippet pairs.
method.task: image-sentence retrieval and image/region caption generation

datasets.name: Flickr8K
datasets.preprocessing: lowercase, drop non-alphanumerics, keep words occurring at least 5 times: 2538 words

datasets.name: MSCOCO
datasets.split: 5,000 validation, 5,000 test, rest train (text mentions 113,000 train images)

datasets.name: Region annotations (new)
datasets.size: 9,000 text snippets on 200 images of the MSCOCO test split (45 per image), average length 2.3 words
datasets.source: collected with AMT, nine annotators per image, five boxes each

models.name: Alignment model (RCNN + BRNN)
models.architecture: RCNN image regions + bidirectional RNN over words, ReLU
models.init_from: CNN pre-trained on ImageNet, finetuned on the 200 ImageNet Detection classes; word embeddings from 300-d word2vec, kept fixed

models.name: Multimodal RNN
models.architecture: simple RNN, image bias bv added at first step only

models.name: Nearest Neighbor
models.architecture: retrieve sentence of nearest training image by L2 on VGGNet fc7

training.objective: alignment: bidirectional max-margin ranking loss with margin 1 (Eq 9); RNN: maximise log probability of next word (softmax)
training.optimizer: alignment: SGD with momentum 0.9; generative RNN: RMSprop
training.dropout: in all layers except recurrent layers; rate not stated
training.seeds: top 5 validation models evaluated independently on test and averaged

other.softmax_bias_init: biases initialised to log probability of word occurrence in training data (Sec 6.5)
other.word_vectors: authors say training them from random init gave little change

inference.decoding: sample or argmax; beam search, e.g. beam size 7

other.beam1_vs_7: beam 1 gives CIDEr 0.61 vs 0.66 at beam 7

metrics.name: Recall@K
metrics.definition: fraction of times a correct item is among top K results

metrics.name: Median rank (Med r)
metrics.definition: median rank of closest ground truth item

metrics.name: BLEU B-n
metrics.definition: BLEU with up to n-grams, coco-caption code, 5 references

eval.protocol: Ranking: top 5 validation models each evaluated on test, averaged; recall std approx 0.5 to 1.0. Captioning: coco-caption scorer. No human evaluation of full-image captions.

limits: Authors: model describes one pixel array at a fixed resolution; image enters only through additive bias; two separately trained models, not end-to-end
Appendix: no explicit counting support; region captions lack context; quality drops for rare concepts
After submission the authors found LSTMs consistently better than their RNN
Retrieval uses AlexNet-class features while captioning uses VGGNet
Table 2 caption says 1,000 test images though the COCO test split is 5,000; learning rate, dropout rate, weight decay, epochs and MRF beta are not stated
The paper never uses the name Karpathy split and names no venue in the PDF

lineage.note: builds on its ranking objective, simplified; BRNN replaces dependency trees
lineage.quote: We build on the approach of Karpathy et al. [24]
